responseText:
I can’t give exact revenue numbers without seeing the chart or the underlying data. Any figures I invent would be guesses. I’m happy to compute exact (or close) values if you either attach the image or provide a few measurements. Briefly:

Why I can’t produce numbers now
- You didn’t attach the chart and I can’t inspect it. Without the image or a known numeric scale (e.g., value of one gridline or the chart min/max), I cannot map bar heights to revenue amounts.

How you can get exact/approximate revenues yourself (quick methods)
1. Provide the chart image (preferred): attach the screenshot and I’ll read/estimate the values.
2. If you can’t attach, give me these numbers (you can get them with any image editor that shows pixel coordinates):
   - y_top: y-coordinate (pixels) of the top of the plot area (where the top gridline is).
   - y_bottom: y-coordinate (pixels) of the bottom of the plot area (x‑axis).
   - For each month (Jan–Jun) give y_bar: the y-coordinate of the top of that month’s bar.
   - axis_min and axis_max: the numeric values corresponding to y_bottom and y_top (if you know them). If you only know one gridline value, give that and indicate which gridline it is.
3. If you know the numeric value of ONE gridline (e.g., each gridline = $50k), tell me which gridline and its value; I can infer the rest.

Formula I’ll use once you supply measurements
- proportion = 1 - (y_bar - y_top) / (y_bottom - y_top)
- revenue = axis_min + proportion * (axis_max - axis_min)

Notes on accuracy and uncertainty
- Results will be approximate because you’re extracting from an image; provide higher-resolution screenshots for better accuracy.
- If you can supply the underlying data (CSV/Excel) or export the chart data from the source, that yields exact numbers.

If you want, paste the pixel coordinates and axis min/max here (or attach the image) and I’ll compute the six monthly revenues.
